messages.content: Write the About page for a company that makes scheduling software for medical clinics. Around 250 words.

output:
Here's the draft. I used a placeholder name and bracketed the facts I can't know — swap those before publishing.

## About

We started **[Company]** after watching a front-desk manager keep a paper waitlist taped beside a $40,000 practice management system. The software did almost everything. It just couldn't tell her who to call when the 2:15 canceled.

That gap is our whole business.

[Company] runs scheduling for medical clinics: the appointment book, and also the work around it that eats a receptionist's afternoon. Waitlist backfill. Recall reminders for the patient who was supposed to come back in six months and didn't. Provider templates that survive a physician moving their Thursdays. Room and equipment holds, so nobody double-books the ultrasound.

Our customers are independent and small-group practices, usually two to forty providers — family medicine, dermatology, physical therapy, behavioral health. Big enough to feel scheduling pain. Too small to have an IT department to throw at it.

A few positions we've committed to:

**No per-message fees on reminders.** Billing a clinic by the text encourages it to send fewer, and fewer reminders means more empty chairs.

**We integrate instead of replacing.** Your EHR stays where it is. We won't ask a practice to migrate ten years of charts to fix its calendar.

**Support picks up the phone**, and the people on it have worked a front desk.

We're [N] people, [bootstrapped] since [year], working out of [city]. We're HIPAA compliant and sign a BAA before you send us a single patient record.

If your schedule is currently held together by a whiteboard and one person's memory, call us. [phone]

---

Two notes: the opening anecdote should be replaced with your actual founding story if you have one — a real specific beats a plausible one. And the "positions we've committed to" block only works if all three are true; drop any that aren't rather than softening them.
